angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 272,019 km at 20.39 pc = 0.18 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 49.0555 +/- 0.0247 mas (same row, RUWE 1.24): 20.39 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.391 +/- 0.02 solar radii from Shporer et al. 2020, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of GJ 1252 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020ApJ...890L...7S/abstract): 272,019 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.381 +/- 0.019 solar masses from Shporer et al. 2020, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of GJ 1252 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020ApJ...890L...7S/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3458 +/- 140 K from Shporer et al. 2020, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of GJ 1252 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020ApJ...890L...7S/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Shporer et al. 2020, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of GJ 1252 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020ApJ...890L...7S/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/gj-1252.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.835, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
